lines.trans: See you soon!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite having no -a ending; means ground, land, or indoor floor.

examples.trans: The floor is clean and dry now.
Set the box on the floor for a moment.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: باردة, plural: باردين).

examples.trans: Here, drink a glass of cold water.
My hands were cold from the rain.

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects old houses.
Amman has beautiful architectural heritage.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Abstract noun from حمى, to protect; in the construct state it is pronounced himaayit (حماية التراث heritage protection).

examples.trans: This cream is protection from the sun.
Protection matters for old houses.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خزاين.

examples.trans: The clean towels are in the linen closet.
We locked the suitcase inside the closet.

meanings.note: One of the four seasons: صيف summer, خريف autumn, شتا winter, ربيع spring.

examples.trans: Spring in Amman is short and lovely.
In spring we go out to the hills.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسايل.

examples.trans: An official letter arrived at noon.
We read the letter line by line.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سقوف.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is high and beautiful.
I slept well under the attic ceiling.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسكر, بيسكر).

examples.trans: He said thank you and hung up!
Did you shut off the main water valve?

meanings.note: Takes the thing first and the name after it: بيسموها 'غرفة الشاي' 'they call it the tea room'. Related to اسم, name.

examples.text: سموا البنت ياسمين على اسم ستها.
examples.trans: They named the girl Yasmin after her grandmother.
What do you call this in Arabic?

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Active participle of شاف ('to see'), standard in Jordanian for 'I see / do you see?'.

examples.text: شايفة رسمة المفتاح الدهبي فوق الباب!
examples.trans: I see the painted golden key above the door!
Do you see the yellow light in the attic window?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, شتا means both the winter season and rain.

examples.trans: Winter water is very cold in the morning.
I love the sound of winter rain on the window.

meanings.note: Singulative شجرة ('a tree', feminine), collective شجر ('trees').

examples.trans: We placed the table under the old tree.
We hear the rustle of tree leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شراشف.

examples.trans: We spread a clean white cloth on the table.
I brought fresh sheets from the closet.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite no -a ending.

examples.trans: The warm sun came out after the rain.
Read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Levantine word for slatted window shutters, used as a collective: الشيش مسكر 'the shutters are closed'.

examples.trans: Close the shutters, the sun is strong.
Green shutters suit the house.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصلح, بيصلح).

examples.trans: I fix pipes and chairs.
Yesterday you fixed the old heater.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلب, بيطلب).

examples.trans: The postman just asked for my signature.

examples.text: طلبت منه يقابلك هون يوم الجمعة؟
examples.trans: Did you ask him to meet you here on Friday?

meanings.note: Used to describe a tall person or a long object.

examples.text: في رجال طويل واقف عند البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a tall man standing by the gate.
Three years was a long time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطل, بيطل).

examples.text: مازن بيطل من ورا الستارة كل دقيقة!
examples.trans: Mazen peeks from behind the curtain every minute!
The window overlooks the courtyard and the tree.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عمام.

examples.trans: I visited my uncle's house on Friday.
My cousin helped me move the things.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The primary interrogative word for quantity, price, or duration in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
Look how peaceful the sky is!

meanings.note: Verbal noun referring to the act of reading or, more broadly, academic studying.

examples.trans: Reading before sleep relaxes me.
My son loves reading.

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كافيهات.

examples.trans: We opened a small café in the house courtyard.
The morning café serves all the neighbours.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Commonly used in Jordanian Arabic instead of the MSA word 'mughlaq'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, is the door locked?
The main water valve is shut off now.

meanings.note: Plural-form noun that is THE everyday Jordanian/Levantine word for money.

examples.trans: Take cash from the box for the shop.
We saved money for annual maintenance.

meanings.note: Describes a rainy day, season or night (يوم ممطر 'a rainy day').

examples.trans: It was a cold, rainy day.
Winter this year is very rainy.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: From نور, light. Also a warm compliment to a guest: البيت منور! 'the house shines (with you)!'.

examples.trans: The room is bright in the morning.
Welcome, your visit lights up the house!

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ناس.

examples.trans: You are kind, generous people.
Morning coffee brings people together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical dot, a score point, or a drop of liquid.

examples.trans: Not a single drop of juice got on the table!

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من الشوربة السخنة.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the hot soup.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقط, بينقط).

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water on your clean floor.
The pipe stopped dripping.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

meanings.note: Extremely common adverb used to express similarity or concluding a statement.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
And after that, where do I go?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

وسع.gloss: to fit; hold; have room for

meanings.en: to fit; hold; have room for
meanings.note: Says how much a place holds: السيارة بتوسع خمس أشخاص 'the car fits five people'. Related to واسع, wide.

examples.trans: The bag doesn't hold all the books.
The table easily fits six.

meanings.note: Takes ب- for the thing promised: وعدته بغرفة 'I promised him a room'.

examples.text: خليني أحزر. وعدت حدا بغرفة مش موجودة عندنا؟
examples.trans: Let me guess. You promised somebody a room we do not have?
I promised you lemon cake on Friday.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!
